title: Make Magic Expensive Without Using Mana

voice.direction: A calm, warm guide. The hook is a real, slightly uneasy question. Each spell line is two beats: the deed, then the price, softer. 'Her sister is a stranger' is tender, not tragic. 'Is the next spell worth it?' is a genuine question, left hanging. The lesson is clear and sure; the comment CTA friendly. No trailer voice.

lines.text: What if every spell stole one of your memories?
Wren keeps a ledger of what she still remembers.
She stills a storm. Her first snow is gone.
She breaks a fever. Her mother's name fades.
One more spell, and her sister is a stranger.
Only her own name is left. Is the next spell worth it?
Years, warmth, a sense: a real price makes every spell a choice.
Comment the strangest price someone could pay for magic.

lesson: Magic doesn't need mana to be expensive. A spell can cost strength, time, years of life, warmth, a sense, social standing, rare materials, emotional stability or a memory. The best price is one the caster truly values, so every spell becomes a decision: is this worth what it takes?

Wren keeps a ledger of what she still remembers. She stills a storm, and her first snow is gone. She breaks a fever, and her mother's name fades. One more spell, and her sister is a stranger. Now only her own name is left. Is the next spell worth it?
